cases.issue_title: The search box of the CSV viewer shows `-/-` while its query matches cells
cases.issue_body: ## Description In the CSV and TSV viewer, the document search box shows `-/-` beside the query for every query, also when cells match. The viewer highlights the matching cells and navigation works, but the box does not show how many cells match or which match is current. It works in other file types. The box also shows `-/-` when nothing matches, so it is quite confusing to users. ## Reproduce 1. Save this file as `fruits.csv`: ``` fruit,colour,price apple,red,1.20 banana,yellow,0.50 apple,green,1.10 cherry,red,3.00 pineapple,brown,2.50 ``` 2. Open it in JupyterLab, which shows it in the CSV viewer. 3. Click in the grid, press Ctrl+F and type `apple`. 4. Press Enter. After step 3 the cell of row 1 is the current match, and the cells of rows 3 and 5 are other matches. After step 4 the current match is row 3. After both steps the box shows `-/-`: The same file opened with Open With > Editor shows `1/3` for the same query: ## Expected behavior The box shows the position of the current match and the number of matches, as it does for a text file: `1/3` after step 3, and `2/3` after step 4. ## Context - Operating System and version: Ubuntu - Browser and version: Chrome - JupyterLab version: 4.6.4

cases.issue_title: Console tab tooltip shows "Last Execution: undefined" instead of the timestamp
cases.issue_body: ## Description The tab tooltip of a code console shows `Last Execution: undefined` instead of the time of the last execution. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open JupyterLab and create a console (File → New → Console). 2. Run any code, e.g. `print("hello")`. 3. Hover over the console tab title. ## Expected behavior The tooltip shows the formatted time of the last execution, like it does for "Connected": ``` Name: Console 1 Directory: / Kernel: Python 3 (ipykernel) Connected: 10/1/26, 3:16 AM Last Execution: 10/1/26, 3:18 AM ``` ## Actual behavior ``` Name: Console 1 Directory: Kernel: Python 3 (ipykernel) Connected: 10/1/26, 3:16 AM Last Execution: undefined ``` **Screenshot:** ## Possible cause In [`packages/console/src/panel.ts#L362-L364`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/main/packages/console/src/panel.ts#L362-L364), the string is built without the formatted time argument: ```ts if (executed) { caption += trans.__('\nLast Execution: %1'); } ``` ## Suggested fix ```ts if (executed) { caption += trans.__( '\nLast Execution: %1', Time.format(executed.toISOString()) ); } ``` I'm happy to open a PR for this. ## Context and reproduction checklist - [x] Reproduced in a clean environment with no third-party extensions - [x] Searched the issue tracker for duplicates (none found for console tab caption / last execution) **Environment** - OS: macOS 27.0 (Build 26A428) - Browser: Google Chrome 144.0.7559.97 - JupyterLab version: 4.5.6 (also reproduced on source build from `main` at commit `ca6acfbe41`) - Notebook version: 7.5.5 - Python: 3.14.3 - ipykernel: 7.2.0 - IPython: 9.11.0

cases.issue_title: Button attached to semantic commands are always visibles
cases.issue_body:
## Description

The semantic commands cannot be hidden, probably because of an implementation error.

https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/463fa674984f9a72dd29c30e25c134ed5ffbf965/packages/application/src/utils.ts#L184-L191

If `isVisible` is set to false, then it fallback to ` || (defaultValues.isVisible ?? true)`, which led to `true` if there is no default value.


## Reproduce

- open a notebook
- select a cell
- in the dev tool (console)
  - removing a button not associated to a semantic command works
  ```
  jupyterapp.commands._commands.get('notebook:cut-cell').isVisible = () => false
  jupyterapp.commands.notifyCommandChanged('notebook:cut-cell')
  ```
  - removing a button associated to a semantic command doesn't
  ```
  jupyterapp.commands._commands.get('notebook:run-cell-and-select-next').isVisible = () => false
  jupyterapp.commands.notifyCommandChanged('notebook:run-cell-and-select-next')
  ```

## Expected behavior

The button to be hidden if expected.

## Context

Observed in https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/pull/19707 when trying to hide the notebook toolbar buttons.

The same error are also on `isEnabled` and `isToggled`, but fall back on `false` instead of `true`, so it kind of work (if it is `false` -> fallback to `false`)

## Suggestion

Looking if the `isVisible` has a length before falling back to the default.

```ts
    isVisible: () => {
      const isVisible = reduceAttribute('isVisible');
      return (
        isVisible.length > 0
          ? !isVisible.some(visible => visible === false)
          : (defaultValues.isVisible ?? true)
      );
```

cases.issue_title: Pressing tab doesnt insert tabs, shows autocomplete instead.
cases.issue_body:
## Description

Is it possible to prevent the [tab] key from doing autocomplete/suggestions in notebook, and instead add a tab, as expected?

I tried adding "disabled" : true to various entries in the shortcuts.jupyterlab-settings file, but it doesn’t seem to have any effect until using a beta as suggested in the discourse link below.

Code completion is not enabled, (default) in the jupyterlab settings window, so I’m not even sure what is firing the dropdown tooltips.

This is not a question of line indentation, which works. I want the ability to tab the = signs on successive lines so that they line up - with tabs, not spaces.

First two lines are tabbed as desired by copy-pasting tab characters, so tabs are possible, but pressing tab on the next line shows this annoying dropdown instead.

![image](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/assets/59213467/64df8027-5da2-414a-8ffe-e5e22f0fd13e)

With the beta and json disabling tabs using json below, the behaviour changes to: pressing tab activates the notebook's tab in the tab status bar 
![image](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/assets/59213467/7000e5e3-7c78-471d-a656-cf8bbceaca7f)

```json
        {
            "command": "completer:invoke-console",
            "selector": ".jp-CodeConsole-promptCell .jp-mod-completer-enabled",
            "keys": [
                "Tab"
            ],
            "disabled": true
        },
        {
            "command": "completer:invoke-notebook",
            "selector": ".jp-Notebook.jp-mod-editMode .jp-mod-completer-enabled",
            "keys": [

            "disabled": true

            "command": "completer:invoke-file",
            "selector": ".jp-FileEditor .jp-mod-completer-enabled",
            "keys": [
                "Tab"
            ],
            "disabled": true
        }
```

Open a notebook, in a code block type a word, space, then tab.

## Expected behavior

\t tab character is inserted

cases.issue_title: Pager panel(help) renders kernel-supplied MIME data with `trusted: true`
cases.issue_body:
## Problem

[`activatePageHandler`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1554-L1629) wraps a kernel `source: "page"` payload in
[`MimeModel({ ..., trusted: true })`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1618). [`renderHTML`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/rendermime/src/renderers.ts#L21-L78) only sanitizes when
[`trusted` is false](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/rendermime/src/renderers.ts#L47), so a `text/html` pager bundle skips the sanitizer and
its inline scripts are executed via [`evalInnerHTMLScriptTags`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/rendermime/src/renderers.ts#L2055-L2081), in the
JupyterLab origin, with no click.

Route: `execute_reply` → [`source: "page"`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/outputarea/src/widget.ts#L885) → [`handlePage`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1586) →
[`MimeModel(trusted: true)`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1618) → [`renderHTML`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/rendermime/src/renderers.ts#L59-L61).

The same handler also calls [`preferredMimeType(mimeData, 'any')`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1598)
unconditionally, which [skips the safe-factory check](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/rendermime/src/registry.ts#L105-L129) and prefers `text/html`
over the `text/plain` that pager payloads are required to carry. The
ordinary output path gets this right [`model.trusted ? 'any' : 'ensure'`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/outputarea/src/widget.ts#L663-L666).

[`helpInBottomPanel`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/schema/tracker.json#L903-L908) defaults to `false` here, but Jupyter Notebook
[overrides it to `true`](https://github.com/jupyter/notebook/blob/v7.7.0a1/packages/application-extension/src/settingconnector.ts#L33-L37) as of `v7.7.0a1` (on PyPI, pinned to
`@jupyterlab/*` `~4.7.0-alpha.1`), so opt-in isn't a mitigation
downstream. Scope is otherwise limited: landed in #18179 (4.7.0a0),
absent from 4.5.x / 4.6.x and from `notebook` ≤ 7.6.2.

## Solution

Sanitize unconditionally. In [`activatePageHandler`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/src/index.ts#L1554-L1629), derive `trusted` once as
`false` and use it for both the MIME selection and the model:

- `preferredMimeType(mimeData, trusted ? 'any' : 'ensure')`
- `new MimeModel({ data: mimeData, metadata, trusted })`

Pager payloads aren't saved into the notebook document, so there's no
signature and no trust state to derive a per-case decision from — the
only options are "always" or "never", and "always" means trusting
kernel-controlled data. Docstrings need no JS, so the UX cost is zero. If
some pager content later does need trusted rendering, that decision must
come from JupyterLab's content-trust state, never from the kernel bundle.

Regression test: [`@jupyterlab/notebook-extension`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/packages/notebook-extension/package.json) has no test setup, so
this belongs in [`galata/test/jupyterlab/notebook-trust.test.ts`](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/blob/7848d05af740c18b5950a8d1b90e2ed580af8260/galata/test/jupyterlab/notebook-trust.test.ts) with
`helpInBottomPanel: true`, deliver a `source: "page"` payload carrying
`text/html` plus a marker script and assert the marker stays unset and no
script node survives; keep coverage for ordinary pager HTML rendering and
for the default-disabled fallback path.

## Related

- #18179: the PR that added the bottom-panel pager
- [Jupyter messaging spec: pager payloads](https://jupyter-client.readthedocs.io/en/latest/messaging.html#payloads-deprecated)
- [JupyterLab notebook trust model](https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/notebook.html)
- [`jupyter/notebook` setting override](https://github.com/jupyter/notebook/blob/v7.7.0a1/packages/application-extension/src/settingconnector.ts#L33-L37)

## Description The PyPI extension manager fails to inspect `package.json` from `.tar.gz` source distributions after an extension install. cases.issue_title: getCookie throws SecurityError in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so the websocket never opens
cases.issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit can't open its websocket when the app runs in an iframe sandboxed without `allow-same-origin`. That frame's document has an opaque origin, and reading `document.cookie` there throws `SecurityError`. `getCookie` in `frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts` reads it without a try/catch. `WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens` calls `getCookie("_streamlit_xsrf")` on every connect, even after `claimHostAuthToken()` has returned a token. The error makes `connectToWebSocket` reject before the handshake starts, and the frame stays blank.

`localStorageAvailable()`, a few lines below `getCookie`, already wraps its storage access in a try/catch. The cookie helpers need the same guard.

We sandbox each embedded app without `allow-same-origin` so that it gets its own opaque origin and can't reach the parent page or another embedded app.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
`app.py`:


import streamlit as st
st.write("hello from streamlit")


`host/index.html`:


<!doctype html>
<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="http://localhost:8599/" width="800" height="400"></iframe>
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `streamlit run app.py --server.port 8599 --server.enableCORS false --server.enableXsrfProtection false --browser.gatherUsageStats false`.
2. Serve the host page with `python -m http.server 8598 -d host`.
3. Open `http://localhost:8598/` in Chromium.

Two things unrelated to this bug get in the way first. Streamlit sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on `/static/`, so the opaque-origin document can't load the module scripts. On loopback, Chromium's Local Network Access check also blocks the websocket. I got past both in Playwright with:

```js
await page.context().grantPermissions(['local-network-access']);
await page.route('http://localhost:8599/**', async r => {
  const res = await r.fetch();
  await r.fulfill({ response: res, headers: { ...res.headers(), 'access-control-allow-origin': '*' } });
});
await page.goto('http://localhost:8598/');
```


### Expected Behavior

`getCookie` returns `undefined` when the document can't read cookies. The handshake goes ahead with the host auth token or the placeholder, and the app renders. With the guard below patched into the 1.65.0 bundle, the frame shows "hello from streamlit".


### Current Behavior

```
SecurityError: Failed to read the 'cookie' property from 'Document': The document is sandboxed and lacks the 'allow-same-origin' flag.
    at wT (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:26:87723)
    at aE.getSessionTokens (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:29:1763)
    at async aE.connectToWebSocket (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:29:2122)
```

No websocket request goes out and the frame stays blank.


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (also 1.56.0)
- Python version: 3.12.14
- Operating system: Linux
- Browser: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (headless)


### Additional Information

Three call sites read the cookie:

- `WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens`, on every connect.
- `DefaultStreamlitEndpoints.csrfRequest`, for file upload and delete when XSRF protection is on.
- `MetricsManager.getAnonymousId`, when usage stats are on. It then calls `setCookie` in `frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts`, which writes `document.cookie` without a guard and throws the same way.

A sandboxed frame can't hold the `_streamlit_xsrf` cookie, so it needs `server.enableXsrfProtection=false`. #16476 gives the same advice for cross-origin pages, and this fix doesn't change that.

A possible fix is to guard both helpers:

```diff
--- a/frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts
+++ b/frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts
 export function getCookie(name: string): string | undefined {
-  const r = document.cookie.match(`\\b${name}=([^;]*)\\b`)
+  let cookies: string
+  try {
+    cookies = document.cookie
+  } catch {
+    // A frame sandboxed without allow-same-origin has no cookie access.
+    return undefined
+  }
+  const r = cookies.match(`\\b${name}=([^;]*)\\b`)
   return r ? r[1] : undefined
 }
--- a/frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts
+++ b/frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts
-  document.cookie = `${name}=${value};${expirationStr}path=/`
+  try {
+    document.cookie = `${name}=${value};${expirationStr}path=/`
+  } catch {
+    // A frame sandboxed without allow-same-origin has no cookie access.
+  }
```

cases.issue_title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
cases.issue_body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary An app that imports an inline `st.components.v2.component(...)` from another module works under `streamlit run`, but in a test suite only the first `AppTest` that imports that module can render it: every later `AppTest` in the same Python process records `StreamlitAPIException: Component '' is not registered.` in `at.exception`. If anything imports the module before the first `AppTest` runs (a `conftest.py`, another test), that one fails too, so results depend on test order. A component defined in the script body itself is not affected, because it registers again on every run. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # my_component.py import streamlit as st greeting = st.components.v2.component("greeting", html="

hi

") # app.py from my_component import greeting greeting(key="g") # test_app.py from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def test_first_apptest_renders_the_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value def test_second_apptest_renders_the_same_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Put the three files in one directory. 2. Run `pytest test_app.py`. ### Expected Behavior Both tests pass, the same way `streamlit run app.py` renders the component every time. ### Current Behavior ``` E AssertionError: Component 'greeting' is not registered. 1 failed, 1 passed ``` The first test passes and the second fails. Each test passes when run on its own. If `import my_component` is added at the top of `test_app.py`, both fail. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0) - Python version: 3.14.7 - Operating System: macOS 27.0 - Browser: n/a (AppTest) ### Additional Information **Why it happens.** `st.components.v2.component()` registers the definition once, when it is called (normally at module import), into `get_bidi_component_manager()`. That is the active runtime's registry, or a throwaway local `BidiComponentManager` when no runtime exists. `AppTest` creates one `BidiComponentManager` per instance (reused across that instance's reruns) and only runs `discover_and_register_components()` on it, which scans installed component packages. Python caches the module, so later instances never re-run the `component()` call, and the name is missing from their registry. **Workaround.** Make the module re-import inside each test's run: ```python # conftest.py import sys import pytest @pytest.fixture(autouse=True) def reimport_component_module(): sys.modules.pop("my_component", None) ``` With this fixture both tests pass. Replacing the component callable with a stub in tests also works. **Suggested fix.** `_mount_component` closes over only `component_key` and `isolate_styles`, but `_create_component_callable()` has the raw `html`, `css` and `js` in scope. If it kept them, `_mount_component` could register the definition into the current registry when the name is missing there, before mounting. File-backed definitions would need their paths resolved against that registry. Alternatively, keep a process-level record of inline definitions and seed each new `AppTest` registry from it. **Related.** #15484 (AppTest did not discover installed CCv2 components) and #14274 (AppTest `TypeError` with CCv2) are both closed. #14274's reproducer used this same imported-module pattern with a single test. The regression test added with its fix (#14301) defines the component inside `AppTest.from_function`, so it registers again on every run and does not cover this case.

Since 1.65.0, looking up any unknown attribute on the `streamlit` module (even `hasattr(st, "x")` or `getattr(st, "x", None)`) imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` and `difflib`. Code that iterates over `sys.modules` while probing module attributes then fails with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. This broke our whole test suite at setup after upgrading from 1.64.0.

import sys
import streamlit

[m for m in sys.modules.values() if getattr(m, "date", None) is not None]
```

As in 1.64.0: the lookup returns the default, and no module is imported.

### Current Behavior

```
RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
```

The module `__getattr__` added in #16912 imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` on every miss, including lookups that only probe with a default:

```python
import sys, streamlit
before = set(sys.modules)
hasattr(streamlit, "date")                 # False, as expected
print(sorted(set(sys.modules) - before))   # ['difflib', 'streamlit.command_suggestions']
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes, this used to work in a previous version (1.64.0).

### Debug info

- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: n/a

- import `streamlit.command_suggestions` eagerly (or once, at first use outside `__getattr__`);

cases.issue_title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
cases.issue_body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

cases.issue_title: Dialog crashes on keydown events without a key
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

`st.dialog` with `dismissible=False` attaches a capture-phase document `keydown` listener that calls `e.key.toLowerCase()` without checking that `key` is a string. A synthetic `keydown` with no `key` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`.

This is the same event class as #17082 (`GlobalHotkeys`), but a separate listener. #17082 / PR #17105 only guards `GlobalHotkeys`. The dialog handler still throws while a non-dismissible dialog is open.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Open a non-dismissible dialog (`st.dialog(..., dismissible=False)`).
2. Dispatch:

```js
document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
```

Expected: ignored (there is no key to match as `r`).
Actual: uncaught TypeError from `Dialog.tsx` `handleRKeySuppress`.

### Notes

- The listener is only attached while a non-dismissible dialog is open (`capture=true`).
- Do not `preventDefault` / `stopImmediatePropagation` when there is no string `key` — that would treat the event as an R-key suppress.
- Related: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17082
- Related PR: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17105

cases.issue_body:
### Checklist

    - [x] I searched the existing issues and pull requests for this bug.
    - [x] I reproduced this on Streamlit 1.63.0 and confirmed the same unguarded code is present on the current develop branch.

    ### Summary

    The global shortcut handler assumes every dispatched keydown/keyup event has a string key. Browser integrations, test harnesses, embedded hosts, or extensions can dispatch an Event without the KeyboardEvent key field. In that case, GlobalHotkeys calls toLowerCase on undefined and throws an uncaught TypeError.

    ### Minimal reproduction

    Run any Streamlit app, open the browser console after the app loads, and execute:

    ~~~js
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keyup"))
    ~~~

    The first event reaches GlobalHotkeys.handleKeyDown and calls normalizeKey(event.key). The second reaches handleKeyUp and does the same. Because Event has no key property, normalizeKey receives undefined and key.toLowerCase() throws.

    A plain DOM Event is intentional here: event listeners can receive synthetic events from browser hosts and integrations despite the TypeScript annotation. The handler should be defensive at this external boundary.

    ### Current implementation

    In frontend/app/src/components/GlobalHotkeys/GlobalHotkeys.tsx:

    ~~~ts
    function normalizeKey(key: string): string {
    return key === "Escape" || key === "Esc" ? "esc" : key.toLowerCase()
    }

    const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }

    const handleKeyUp = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
    const normalizedKey = normalizeKey(event.key)
    // ...
    }
    ~~~

    ### Expected behavior

    Malformed or non-keyboard keydown/keyup events without a string key should be ignored without throwing. Normal keyboard shortcuts should continue to work.

    ### Suggested fix

    Guard both handlers before normalization, for example:

    ~~~ts
    if (typeof event.key !== "string") {
    return
    }
    ~~~

    Alternatively, make normalizeKey accept unknown and return undefined for invalid values, with callers returning early.

    ### Regression test

    Add cases in GlobalHotkeys.test.tsx that dispatch keydown and keyup events without key and assert that no exception is thrown and no shortcut callback runs.

    ### Environment

    - Streamlit: 1.63.0
    - Also present on the current develop branch as of 2026-09-22
    - Browser: Chromium

cases.issue_title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
cases.issue_body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary This is a documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug. The behavior is by design (#15790, closing #15005), and this report does not ask to change it. It asks for the two places that describe `delta` to match it. The `delta` docstring gives four unqualified rules ([metric.py lines 150-158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L150-L158)): no arrow for `None` or an empty string, "if the delta is zero, no arrow is shown and the delta is gray", red and down for "a negative number or starts with a minus sign", otherwise green and up. `delta_color="normal"` repeats "gray when zero" ([metric.py line 170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L170)) and `delta_arrow="auto"` says "no arrow is shown if `delta` is zero" ([metric.py line 269](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L269)). Those rules treat strings as first-class input (the minus-sign branch exists only for strings), so a reader expects a zero-valued string such as `"0%"` or `"+0.0%"` to be "zero". The implementation defines zero for strings as the literal `"0"` only ([metric.py lines 598-604](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L598-L604)), with the comment "other numeric-looking strings (e.g. `"0.0"`, `"0%"`) stay positive". #15790 added that deliberately, on the basis that string deltas are opaque display text, and locked it in with an anti-regression test. The docstring was not updated to say so, which is the gap. The packaged `developing-with-streamlit` skill widens the gap in practice. Every `st.metric` example in it passes `delta` as a pre-formatted string: [dashboards.md line 17](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L17), [dashboards.md lines 47-49](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L47-L49), and [data-display.md line 363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/data-display.md?plain=1#L363). The skill never mentions zero, so it does not contradict anything, but an agent that follows its examples and then reads the docstring's "gray when zero" will format a flat period as `"0%"` and get a green up-arrow. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python For reference only. This shows the designed behavior, not a bug; it is here so the mismatch with the docstring wording can be seen without reading the source. import streamlit as st col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3) # What the skill's examples lead to for a flat period: col1.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "0%") # green up-arrow col2.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "-0.0%") # red down-arrow # What actually renders neutral: col3.metric("Orders (numeric)", 1400, 0, delta_description="vs last month") "I.e.:" from streamlit.elements.metric import _is_zero_delta for delta in ["0", "0%", "+0.0%", "-0.0%", 0]: repr(delta), _is_zero_delta(delta) # '0' True # '0%' False # '+0.0%' False # '-0.0%' False # 0 True ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Read the `delta` docstring's "if the delta is zero" rule and `delta_color="normal"`'s "gray when zero". 2. `streamlit run` or `uv run streamlit run` the snippet. 3. Compare the first two tiles with the third / see the debug output beneath it. ### Expected Behavior Documentation that states the actual rule: 1. In the `delta` docstring (and the `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` mentions of zero), say that a string delta is displayed as-is and that only the literal string `"0"` is treated as zero; other zero-like strings follow the sign rule (leading minus is negative, anything else is positive). One sentence is enough. 2. In the packaged skill, either show at least one example with a numeric `delta` and qualifier text in `delta_description=`, or add a one-line note next to the string examples that string deltas are never treated as zero. ### Current Behavior The docstring says zero deltas are gray with no qualification about strings. `"0%"` renders as a positive delta with a green up-arrow and `"-0.0%"` as a negative delta with a red down-arrow, which is the designed behavior. The skill's examples are all strings and say nothing about zero. For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a regression and not a behavior change request. Verified on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing): the docstring text, the skill examples, and `_is_zero_delta` are identical in both, and unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information The behavior was settled in #15790: the PR description lists an anti-regression test that `"0.0"`, `"+0"` and `"0%"` "stay green/up", and review confirmed the numbers-versus-strings split as intended. Nothing here asks to reopen that; it asks for the docstring and the skill to describe it. `format=` is not a way around the string question: it is one format applied to both `value` and `delta`, and `"percent"` multiplies by 100, so a tile whose value is a count and whose delta is a percent change cannot be served by a single `format=`. Numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` is the pattern that works, and it is the one the skill could show.

### Summary

When a NumberColumn cell is selected and you type a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.01`), the `.` is silently dropped and the remaining digits are committed as a whole number — `.01` becomes `1`, `.07` becomes `7`. )

Click the Margin cell for row A (shows 12.0000).

### Current Behavior

cases.issue_title: Build hangs forever after 10 page render errors: `renderPages` blocks on `pages <- p` after `errorCollator` calls `Stop`
cases.issue_body:
This report was written by Claude Opus 5.5

## What version of Hugo are you using?

```text
hugo v0.168.0-e27a6760c5547237f87d353aebe0580feadb20f4 linux/amd64 BuildDate=2026-10-13T16:42:50Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
```

## Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes.

## What happened

When a build has 10 or more page render errors, `hugo` sometimes never exits.
It prints no error, uses no CPU, and waits forever. A SIGQUIT dump shows the
page walker in `renderPages` blocked sending to `pages`, and `errorCollator`
blocked on its final send to `errs`. No `pageRenderer` goroutines are left.

The hang is a race. With default settings, the reproducer below hung in 26 of
500 builds on a 16-CPU linux/amd64 machine. With `GOMAXPROCS=1
HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER=2` (the script's defaults; they only change
scheduling), it hung in 30 of 30 builds (3 runs of the script, 10 builds each,
about 50 seconds per run).

## Expected

The build fails promptly and prints the collated render errors.

## Reproducer

POSIX shell. It creates a site in `$(mktemp -d)` whose pages all fail to render
(`.Content` on a nil resource), builds it `RUNS` times, treats a build that
doesn't exit within `LIMIT` seconds as hung, and prints the goroutine dump of
the first hung build (`timeout -s QUIT`). It deletes the site when done.

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Build a site whose pages all fail to render, RUNS times; report builds
# that don't exit within LIMIT seconds and print the first one's goroutines.
HUGO=${HUGO:-hugo}
PAGES=${PAGES:-50}
RUNS=${RUNS:-10}
LIMIT=${LIMIT:-5}
# Scheduling settings that make the race hit almost every time.
# Set both to "" to use Hugo's defaults (the hang is then much rarer).
export GOMAXPROCS="${GOMAXPROCS-1}"
export HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER="${HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER-2}"

dir=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$dir"' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

site=$dir/site
mkdir -p "$site/layouts" "$site/content"
printf 'disableKinds = ["taxonomy", "term", "rss", "sitemap"]\n' > "$site/hugo.toml"
# .Content on a nil resource: every page fails to render.
printf '{{ (resources.Get "missing.svg").Content }}\n' > "$site/layouts/single.html"
cp "$site/layouts/single.html" "$site/layouts/list.html"
i=1
while [ "$i" -le "$PAGES" ]; do
  printf -- '---\ntitle: p%s\n---\n' "$i" > "$site/content/p$i.md"
  i=$((i + 1))
done

"$HUGO" version
echo "GOMAXPROCS=$GOMAXPROCS HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER=$HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER PAGES=$PAGES"
hung=0 n=1
while [ "$n" -le "$RUNS" ]; do
  timeout -s QUIT "$LIMIT" "$HUGO" -s "$site" -d "$dir/public" > "$dir/log" 2>&1
  if [ $? = 124 ]; then
    hung=$((hung + 1))
    echo "build $n: hung (no exit after ${LIMIT}s)"
    [ "$hung" = 1 ] && cp "$dir/log" "$dir/first-hang"
  else
    echo "build $n: exited"
  fi
  n=$((n + 1))
done
echo "hung in $hung of $RUNS builds"
if [ "$hung" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "--- output of first hung build (SIGQUIT goroutine dump) ---"
  cat "$dir/first-hang"
  exit 1
fi
```

Run it with `HUGO=/path/to/hugo sh repro.sh`. For Hugo's default scheduling,
run `GOMAXPROCS= HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER= RUNS=500 sh repro.sh`.

### Example output

From one run of the script above (`HUGO=/path/to/hugo-0.168.0 sh repro.sh`).
The goroutine dump is trimmed to its header and the two blocked goroutines,
with runtime frames and frame addresses removed.

```text

GOMAXPROCS=1 HUGO_NUMWORKERMULTIPLIER=2 PAGES=50
build 1: hung (no exit after 5s)
...
build 10: hung (no exit after 5s)
hung in 10 of 10 builds
--- output of first hung build (SIGQUIT goroutine dump) ---
Start building sites … 
hugo v0.168.0-e27a6760c5547237f87d353aebe0580feadb20f4 linux/amd64 BuildDate=2026-10-13T16:42:50Z VendorInfo=gohugoio

SIGQUIT: quit
...
goroutine 10 gp=0x11c2c5fce3c0 m=nil [chan send]:
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*Site).renderPages.func1({0x2fcd600?, 0x11c2c5d48600?}, {0x2fc04c8?, 0x11c2c6789e30?})

goroutine 16 gp=0x11c2c5bc7680 m=nil [chan send]:

	/root/project/hugo/hugolib/site.go:1577 +0x4c

	/root/project/hugo/hugolib/site.go:1588 +0x170

	/root/project/hugo/hugolib/site_render.go:78 +0x1f
created by github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*Site).renderPages in goroutine 10
	/root/project/hugo/hugolib/site_render.go:78 +0xe5
```

The main goroutine waits in `errgroup.(*Group).Wait` in
`commands.(*hugoBuilder).fullBuild`. The other goroutines are idle runtime and
cache goroutines.

## Analysis

Line numbers are for the v0.168.0 tag.

[`hugolib/site_render.go` L91–L104](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/v0.168.0/hugolib/site_render.go#L91-L104),
the walk handler in `renderPages`, checks for cancellation only before it
blocks:

```go
select {
case <-s.h.Done():
	return radix.WalkStop, nil
default:
	pages <- p // L98
}
```

[`hugolib/site.go` L1574–L1588](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/v0.168.0/hugolib/site.go#L1574-L1588),
`errorCollator`, calls `s.h.Stop()` after `maxErrors` (10) errors (L1583–L1586)
and stops reading `results`. Each `pageRenderer` then sees `Done()` in
`sendErr` on its next error
([`site_render.go` L132–L139](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/v0.168.0/hugolib/site_render.go#L132-L139))
and returns, so nothing reads `pages` any more.

If the walker passed its `Done()` check before `Stop()` and is blocked on the
full `pages` channel (buffered to `numWorkers`, L75), the send at L98 never
completes. The walk never returns, so `close(pages)`, `wg.Wait()` and
`err := <-errs`
([L110–L116](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/v0.168.0/hugolib/site_render.go#L110-L116))
are never reached. The deferred `errs <- ...` in `errorCollator` (`site.go`
L1577, unbuffered `errs`, `site_render.go` L76) then blocks too, and the
collated errors are never returned or printed.

## Suggested fix

Make the send itself select on `Done()`, so the walker can always leave:

```go
select {
case <-s.h.Done():
	return radix.WalkStop, nil
case pages <- p:
}
```

With that, `renderPages` always reaches `<-errs`, so the collator's final send
completes. Making `errs` buffered (`make(chan error, 1)`) would also stop the
collator goroutine blocking if a future change returns early before L116.

$ hugo version
hugo v0.151.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64 BuildDate=2025-10-02T13:30:36Z VendorInfo=brew
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes ## Issue Using a blockquote that extends past the `.Summary` cutoff causes the content below `{{ .Summary }}` to be treated as part of the blockquote until the end of the parent tag. [Reproduction repo](https://github.com/imomaliev/hugo-blockquote-summary-leak) Hugo's `.Summary` may lead to `blockquote` end tag be below cutoff point ## Explanation In most modern browsers this html code will be parsed and rendered without errors ```html

``` Leading to shown in browser as a source ```html

1

``` This is due to [these parsing rules](html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inbody#:~:text=An%20end%20tag%20whose%20tag%20name%20is%20one%20of%3A%20%22address%22%2C%20%22article%22%2C%20%22aside%22%2C%20%22blockquote%22) > An end tag whose tag name is one of: "address", "article", "aside", "blockquote", "button", "center", "details", "dialog", "dir", "div", "dl", "fieldset", "figcaption", "figure", "footer", "header", "hgroup", "listing", "main", "menu", "nav", "ol", "pre", "search", "section", "select", "summary", "ul" > > If the stack of open elements does not have an element in scope that is an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error; ignore the token. > > Otherwise, run these steps: > > Generate implied end tags. > > If the current node is not an HTML element with the same tag name as that of the token, then this is a parse error. > > Pop elements from the stack of open elements until an HTML element with the same tag name as the token has been popped from the stack. ## To Discuss I think the best case scenario is for `.Summary` to handle generation of implied tags. But I am not sure how to do that myself. I did not run a tagged release binary, so I have not confirmed it against one directly, though the code path is unchanged in `tpl/compare/compare.go`. ### What did you expect to see? `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt` and `ge` agreeing with each other. Whatever the rule for comparing an `int` against a `float`, exactly one of `lt`/`eq`/`gt` should hold for a given pair, `le` should mean `lt or eq`, and `ge` should mean `gt or eq`. ### What did you see instead? For `1` against `1.0`, the six functions contradict each other. `le` and `ge` are both true while `lt`, `gt` and `eq` are all false, so the value is reported as neither less than, nor greater than, nor equal to itself. `layouts/index.html`: ```go-html-template eq 1 1.0 = {{ eq 1 1.0 }} ne 1 1.0 = {{ ne 1 1.0 }} lt 1 1.0 = {{ lt 1 1.0 }} le 1 1.0 = {{ le 1 1.0 }} gt 1 1.0 = {{ gt 1 1.0 }} ge 1 1.0 = {{ ge 1 1.0 }} ``` Rendered output: ``` eq 1 1.0 = false ne 1 1.0 = true lt 1 1.0 = false le 1 1.0 = true gt 1 1.0 = false ge 1 1.0 = true ``` `eq` normalises an `int` to `int64` and a `float` to `float64` and then compares them as `any`, so they are never equal. `lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge` go through `compareGet`, which converts both to `float64`, so they compare numerically. The two halves of the API use different rules. Same result for `0` vs `0.0`, `-1` vs `-1.0`, `int64(3)` vs `float64(3)` and `uint(4)` vs `4.0`. Mixed values where the numbers genuinely differ (`1` vs `2.0`) are consistent, so this only shows up when the two are numerically equal. This is adjacent to #3721, which asked for `eq` to be more lenient and was closed by the stale bot in 2018 without a decision. This report is narrower: whichever convention you prefer, the current combination is not self-consistent. I have not sent a patch because the fix is a semantics choice, either making `eq` compare numerically or making `le`/`ge` strict about mixed types, and that is your call. Happy to send a PR once you say which. This issue was written primarily by Claude Code, including the reproduction above.

cases.issue_title: config/allconfig: Improve resilience of hugo mod init
cases.issue_body:
If the project configuration references output formats defined by an imported module, `hugo mod init` fails before it can do its job. For example:

> ERROR failed to create config: unknown output format "print" for kind "section"

The module that defines the output format can't be loaded until the project is initialized, so the command should tolerate unknown output formats rather than refusing to run. Same applies to `defaultOutputFormat`.

Reference: <https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/57512>

cases.issue_title: templates.Defer: identical block bodies in different output formats share one escaping mode, chosen non-deterministically per build
cases.issue_body:
### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)? 
$ hugo version
hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes. ```text hugo v0.165.0-76a5e1880ab46688155b02e99bab9be2a6134492+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-08-12T14:26:28Z VendorInfo=gohugoio ``` Over one run of 40 consecutive builds of the unchanged reproduction site below with that binary, 28 builds published the wrong value in `public/index.html` and 12 published the wrong value in `public/index.txt`. All 40 exited 0, and none printed a warning or an error. ### Summary When two templates belonging to different output formats contain byte-identical `templates.Defer` block bodies, both blocks do execute, each with its own correct output-format context. What they share is the escaping applied inside the block, and which of the two escaping modes survives changes from build to build of an unchanged site. On every build exactly one of the two outputs is therefore wrong: either an HTML page publishes a value raw that it escapes correctly a few characters earlier outside the block, or a plain-text page receives HTML entities. ### Reproduction Three files in an empty directory. No content, no modules, no external tooling. `hugo.toml`: ```toml baseURL = 'https://example.org/' title = 'defer probe' disableKinds = ['page', 'section', 'taxonomy', 'term', 'RSS', 'sitemap', 'robotsTXT'] [outputFormats.probe] mediaType = 'text/plain' baseName = 'index' isPlainText = true [outputs] home = ['html', 'probe'] ``` `layouts/home.html`: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `layouts/home.probe.txt`, byte-identical to `layouts/home.html` (both md5 `c921197a9c8637852e38d94a0352359d`): ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` `OUT[...]` interpolates the value outside the deferred block, `IN[...]` interpolates the same value inside it. Then run `hugo` several times without changing anything, and look at `public/index.html` and `public/index.txt` after each run. ### What happens Two consecutive runs of the same command on the unchanged site, pasted verbatim: ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio INFO build: step process substep collect files 0 files_total 0 pagesources_total 0 resourcesources_total 0 duration 0s INFO build: step process duration 0s INFO build: step assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 1.3703ms INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 509.5µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.8798ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7766ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 4.171ms │ EN ──────────────────┼──── Pages │ 2 Paginator pages │ 0 Non-page files │ 0 Static files │ 0 Processed images │ 0 Aliases │ 0 Cleaned │ 0 Total in 12 ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` ```text $ hugo --logLevel info Start building sites … hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio INFO build: step process substep collect files 0 files_total 0 pagesources_total 0 resourcesources_total 0 duration 513.8µs INFO build: step process duration 513.8µs INFO build: step assemble duration 0s INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat html duration 517.9µs INFO build: step render substep pages site en outputFormat probe duration 517.2µs INFO build: step render pages 2 content 0 duration 1.0351ms INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 2.0736ms INFO build: step postProcess duration 0s INFO build: duration 3.6225ms │ EN ──────────────────┼──── Pages │ 2 Paginator pages │ 0 Non-page files │ 0 Static files │ 0 Processed images │ 0 Aliases │ 0 Cleaned │ 0 Total in 12 ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[<b>&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[<b>&] ``` In the first run the HTML page publishes `&` raw inside the block, a few characters after escaping the same value correctly outside it. In the second run the plain-text page receives `<b>&`. Nothing changed between the two runs. Quantified over builds of the unchanged site, each build a separate one-shot `hugo` invocation: | Hugo version | builds | `index.html` published raw `&` inside the block | `index.txt` published `<b>&` inside the block | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 25 | 15 | | v0.164.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 23 | 17 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build | 40 | 26 | 14 | | v0.165.0, fresh copy of the site per build, second run | 40 | 28 | 12 | | v0.164.0, repeated builds in one directory | 12 | 8 | 4 | | v0.165.0, repeated builds in one directory | 8 | 5 | 3 | In all 180 of those builds the two output formats carried the *same* string inside the block, so exactly one of the two published files was wrong every time; outside the block the value was escaped correctly for its format in every build. ### What I expected Each format's deferred block rendered under that format's own escaping — `IN[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `IN[&]` in `public/index.txt` — and the same result on every build of an unchanged site. The documentation says "The output format, site, and language will be the same, even if the execution is deferred." The output-format *context* does hold up, as the identity-token control below shows; it is the escaping regime that does not follow the output format. ### Controls All of these were run at both v0.164.0 and v0.165.0. **The block really does execute once per output format.** Adding `{{ warnf "DEFER-EXEC-%d" math.Counter }}` to the start of the still byte-identical block body logs two executions in every build: ```text WARN DEFER-EXEC-1 WARN DEFER-EXEC-2 INFO build: step render deferred count 2 duration 1.7497ms --- public/index.html --- OUT[<b>&]IN[&] --- public/index.txt --- OUT[&]IN[&] ``` So this is not one rendering substituted into two files; it is two renderings sharing one escaping mode. **Different `key` values do not separate them.** With `"KH"` in `layouts/home.html` and `"KT"` in `layouts/home.probe.txt`, the block bodies still byte-identical, the escaping stayed shared and kept flipping: 36 builds, 22 with the HTML page wrong and 14 with the plain-text page wrong. **Different block body text does separate them, stably.** Changing the body to `INH[{{ .v }}]` in the HTML template and `INT[{{ .v }}]` in the plain-text template gives the correct per-format result in 36 of 36 builds, with no flip: `INH[<b>&]` in `public/index.html` and `INT[&]` in `public/index.txt`. **The per-format context inside the block is correct.** With the body still byte-identical in both templates, but carrying an output-format identity token next to the value: ```go-html-template {{ $v := "&" }}OUT[{{ $v }}]{{ with (templates.Defer (dict "key" "K" "data" (dict "v" $v))) }}IN[{{ (index page.AlternativeOutputFormats 0).Name }}|{{ .v }}]{{ end }} ``` With exactly two formats configured the single alternative names the *other* one, so `IN[probe|...]` marks the execution that produced the HTML page and `IN[html|...]` the one that produced the plain-text page. That token was correct in 36 of 36 builds, while the escaping of the value beside it in the very same body was shared and flipped across those builds: ```text public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|&] public/index.html OUT[<b>&]IN[probe|<b>&] public/index.txt OUT[&]IN[html|<b>&] ``` ### Where this appears to come from Offered as a lead from reading the source, not as an instrumented finding. `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go`, `handleWith` (v0.164.0, function at line 409) registers the extracted block under a hash of the block body alone, at lines 450-459: ```go inner := withNode.List.CopyList() s := inner.String() ... innerHash := hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(s) deferredID := tpl.HugoDeferredTemplatePrefix + innerHash ... c.deferNodes[deferredID] = inner ``` Nothing about the owning template, its output format or its media type enters that identifier, so two templates in different output formats with the same body produce the same `deferredID`. `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `addDeferredTemplate` (v0.164.0, function at line 916) then keeps only the first registration under that name, and the first owner fixes the parse namespace for whoever comes later: ```go if _, found := t.templatesByPath.Get(name); found { return nil } ... if owner.D.IsPlainText { prototype := t.tns.parseText ... } else { prototype := t.tns.parseHTML ... } ``` That is exactly the escaping regime the two output formats disagree about, and the loser silently inherits the winner's. Which owner gets there first looks order-dependent. `transformTemplates` (function at line 1916) reaches the registrations by ranging `s.templates()` at line 1937, and that iterator's inner loop at line 1784 ranges a `map[nodeKey]*TemplInfo` — the value type of `treeMain`, declared at line 447 — whose iteration order Go randomizes per run. I found no sort on that path. One contrast worth noting: the sibling transform in the same file, `handleWithPartial` (function at line 324), hashes the owning template's name into its identifier at line 335 — `hashing.XxHashFromStringHexEncoded(c.t.Name() + withNodeInnerString)` — while the older defer path does not. I checked the implicated files at v0.164.0, v0.165.0 and master `7b5199fdeff7d7682e9f979f468d55bc7b67b934`: `tpl/tplimpl/templatestore.go`, `tpl/templates/templates.go` and `tpl/template.go` are byte-identical at all three, and `tpl/tplimpl/templatetransform.go` differs at master only outside this path — the `handleWith` lines quoted above are unchanged there, at 405-414. ### A constraint on any fix Hashing the owning template's name into the deferred identifier, the way `handleWithPartial` does, would break something the documentation promises for `key`: "This will, combined with a hash of the template content, be used as a cache key." Two *different layouts of the same output format* with identical bodies and one shared key share a single execution today, and that is worth keeping — at both versions, on a variant of the site above reduced to one output format and with the `page` kind enabled plus one content file, so that `single.html` renders at all, I measured a single `DEFER-EXEC-1` for a `home.html` and a `single.html` written that way, with both pages publishing the shared result. Separating registrations by the property that actually differs here — the owner's `IsPlainText`, or its output format — would fix the escaping while leaving that documented same-format sharing untouched. ### Related, not duplicates - #7774, fixed by #8462 ("Fixes #7774", merged 2021-04-23): per-build nondeterminism in output-format template lookup for shortcodes. Same failure shape, different subsystem, and it predates `templates.Defer`. - #13236: two empty deferred blocks *in the same template* collided on the identifier `__hdeferred/cafc7706cee4572b` and panicked; closed as completed. That is the same body-only identifier, in a different situation — the collision there is inside one template, and the cross-output-format escaping consequence does not come up. I did not find an existing report covering byte-identical `templates.Defer` bodies across output formats. ### What I did not establish - **Which registration wins in any individual build.** I inferred the winner from the escaping in the published output; I did not instrument the running binary to observe the registration. - **Platform generality.** Everything above was measured on one machine, Windows 11, amd64 extended builds. Whether the split differs on another platform or core count is unmeasured. - **Two non-plain-text formats sharing a body.** The escaping observable needs an `isPlainText` format paired with an HTML one, so two HTML-ish formats sharing a body were not tested and the reach across format combinations is unknown.

cases.issue_title: hugo mod npm pack emits a publishable, checkout-named package.json
cases.issue_body:
**TL;DR**: the generated `package.json` has no `"private": true` and a checkout-derived `name`, so committed copies are publishable under names sites don't control. Suggested fix: emit `"private": true` and a stable (ideally scoped) default name.

### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)?

```
hugo v0.165.0-76a5e1880ab46688155b02e99bab9be2a6134492+extended darwin/arm64 BuildDate=2026-08-12T14:26:28Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
```

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes (transcript below is v0.165.0). The behavior is in master's [package_builder.go](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/blob/master/modules/npm/package_builder.go).

### What happened

`hugo mod npm pack` writes `packages/hugoautogen/package.json` with:

- a **name derived from the checkout directory**, so it varies per clone and can be a registry name the site doesn't control, and
- **no `"private": true`**, npm's do-not-publish guard for internal packages.

The file is regenerated wholesale on each run, so hand-set fields don't survive. From a fresh clone of a repo whose committed copy was hand-normalized:

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/google/docsy-example.git site-a && cd site-a
$ grep -E '"(name|version|private)"' packages/hugoautogen/package.json
  "name": "@docsy/hugoautogen",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true
$ hugo mod npm pack
$ grep -E '"(name|version|private)"' packages/hugoautogen/package.json
  "name": "site-a",
  "version": "0.1.0"
```

A sibling clone of the same repo into `site-b` yields `"name": "site-b"`.

### Why it matters

Sites that commit the generated workspace (e.g. so `npm ci` works without running Hugo first) end up carrying a manifest that npm workspace publishing and common release tools treat as publishable by default: `npm publish --dry-run --workspaces` packs it as `site-a@0.1.0`, while with `"private": true` npm skips the workspace. The name variance also churns the committed manifest, and the lockfile's workspace entry, across differently named checkouts.

### What did you expect

The generated internal workspace is non-publishable (`"private": true`) and has a stable, project-controlled default name rather than the checkout directory's basename. Ideally the default is scoped: a bare name can be claimed on the registry by anyone, a scoped one only by the scope owner.

### Workaround

[docsy-example#487](https://github.com/google/docsy-example/pull/487) follows each pack invocation with a single `npm pkg set` line restoring a scoped name and `private`.

Happy to send a PR for the `private` field (and for the name default, if you have a preference for what it should be).

cases.issue_title: GetSortedMapValues reads the map after releasing the read lock, so a concurrent SetInMap aborts the build
cases.issue_body:
### What version of Hugo are you using (`hugo version`)? 
$ hugo version
hugo v0.164.0-ce2470e7012b5ab5fc4e10ebe4027e9f8d9e00dc+extended windows/amd64 BuildDate=2026-07-06T16:39:30Z VendorInfo=gohugoio
### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes. `common/hstore/scratch.go` is byte-identical at `v0.164.0`, at `v0.165.0` and on `master`, and the line numbers cited below are the same in all three. --- `Scratch.GetSortedMapValues` holds the read lock only long enough to fetch the map header out of `c.values`. It releases the lock and then iterates and indexes that map: ```go // common/hstore/scratch.go @ v0.165.0 func (c *Scratch) GetSortedMapValues(key string) any { c.mu.RLock() if c.values[key] == nil { c.mu.RUnlock() return nil } unsortedMap := c.values[key].(map[string]any) c.mu.RUnlock() // L141: lock released here var keys []string for mapKey := range unsortedMap { // L143: map iteration, unlocked keys = append(keys, mapKey) } sort.Strings(keys) sortedArray := make([]any, len(unsortedMap)) // L149: map read, unlocked for i, mapKey := range keys { sortedArray[i] = unsortedMap[mapKey] // L151: map read, unlocked } return sortedArray } ``` `SetInMap` writes into that same map while holding the write lock. A mutex protects a map only when both sides hold it during the access, so `GetSortedMapValues` running concurrently with `SetInMap` is an unsynchronized read against a write. The Go runtime treats that as fatal and aborts the process; it is not a race a program can be built to tolerate. Every other method on this type reads or writes `c.values` under the lock. This one is the outlier: it takes the lock, then does its actual work after releasing it. This is reachable from ordinary templates. `hugo.Store`, `site.Store`, `PAGE.Store` and `SHORTCODE.Store` all return `*hstore.Scratch`, `hugo.Store` is one instance shared across the whole build, and `renderPages` in `hugolib/site_render.go` renders pages concurrently over `config.GetNumWorkerMultiplier()` workers. So a site that collects into a map with `SetInMap` from a partial called per page, and enumerates it with `GetSortedMapValues` from another template, can abort mid-build. `SetInMap` and `GetSortedMapValues` are documented together as a pair on both `hugo.Store` and `site.Store` — the two build-shared scopes — and no Store documentation page mentions concurrency at all, so nothing warns a template author away from that shape. When it does abort, the build stops with a runtime panic rather than a Hugo error, no finished site is produced, and the panic names no template. The same commit will usually build cleanly on the next run, so it reads as flaky CI rather than as a defect. The sibling `Values()` carries a comment warning that using it on a shared `Scratch` "will lead to concurrency issues". `GetSortedMapValues` carries no such warning, which is part of why it reads as the safe way to get a map back out of a store. I have not built a Hugo-site reproduction, because at the site level this is nondeterministic by nature: it needs a shared store written during concurrent page rendering and read while that is still in flight, and when it fires the panic points at no template. The Go-level reproduction below pins the same two calls deterministically. ### Reproduction This uses only the exported API of `common/hstore`; nothing touches the map directly. `go.mod`: ``` module hstorerepro go 1.26.0 require github.com/gohugoio/hugo v0.164.0 ``` Run `go mod tidy` after creating it; that adds nine indirect requirements and the `go.sum` entries. `repro_test.go`: ```go package hstorerepro import ( "sync" "testing" "github.com/gohugoio/hugo/common/hstore" ) // One goroutine enumerates the map through the store's own accessor while // another writes to it through the store's own mutator. Both use only the // exported API; neither ever touches the map directly. func TestGetSortedMapValuesRacesSetInMap(t *testing.T) { s := hstore.NewScratch() s.SetInMap("k", "seed", "seed") var wg sync.WaitGroup wg.Add(2) go func() { defer wg.Done() for i := 0; i < 100000; i++ { s.SetInMap("k", string(rune('a'+i%26)), i) } }() go func() { defer wg.Done() for i := 0; i < 100000; i++ { _ = s.GetSortedMapValues("k") } }() wg.Wait() } ``` `go test -count=1 .` fails on every run here, with go1.26.2 on windows/amd64. It lands on either unlocked access. Both transcripts below are complete single runs, with only the module-cache and temporary-directory prefixes shortened to `...`: ``` fatal error: concurrent map read and map write goroutine 10 [running]: internal/runtime/maps.fatal({0x7ff6230b07fc?, 0x30?}) C:/Program Files/Go/src/runtime/panic.go:1181 +0x18 github.com/gohugoio/hugo/common/hstore.(*Scratch).GetSortedMapValues(0x4ce82e38820, {0x7ff6230bd980, 0x1}) .../hugo@v0.164.0/common/hstore/scratch.go:151 +0x30d hstorerepro.TestGetSortedMapValuesRacesSetInMap.func2() .../hstore-repro/repro_test.go:30 +0x65 created by hstorerepro.TestGetSortedMapValuesRacesSetInMap in goroutine 8 .../hstore-repro/repro_test.go:27 +0x135 FAIL hstorerepro 0.595s FAIL ``` ``` fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write goroutine 10 [running]: internal/runtime/maps.fatal({0x7ff72f4523b8?, 0x7ff72f264301?}) C:/Program Files/Go/src/runtime/panic.go:1181 +0x18 internal/runtime/maps.(*Iter).Next(0xf18943adf18?) C:/Program Files/Go/src/internal/runtime/maps/table.go:819 +0x86 github.com/gohugoio/hugo/common/hstore.(*Scratch).GetSortedMapValues(0xf18942ba820, {0x7ff72f45d980, 0x1}) .../hugo@v0.164.0/common/hstore/scratch.go:143 +0x17f hstorerepro.TestGetSortedMapValuesRacesSetInMap.func2() .../hstore-repro/repro_test.go:30 +0x65 created by hstorerepro.TestGetSortedMapValuesRacesSetInMap in goroutine 8 .../hstore-repro/repro_test.go:27 +0x135 FAIL hstorerepro 0.578s FAIL ``` Line 143 is the `range` over the map and line 151 is the index into it, so both of the accesses that can abort were reached. The `len(unsortedMap)` at line 149 is a third unlocked read; it does not trigger the runtime check. ### Suggested fix Hold the read lock across the whole function, so the iteration and the indexing happen under it: ```go func (c *Scratch) GetSortedMapValues(key string) any { c.mu.RLock() defer c.mu.RUnlock() if c.values[key] == nil { return nil } // ... unchanged } ``` This adds no nested locking and no re-entrancy, and the function already returns a freshly allocated slice. `sort.Strings` then runs on a local slice while the read lock is held, which blocks writers for that span; if that is unwanted, copying the map into the slice under the lock and sorting after releasing it gives the same guarantee without it. This is not a request to make `Scratch` concurrency-safe in general — it already is, by design and by every other method on the type. It is one function that acquires the right lock and then does its work outside it. A short comment on the method saying the read is safe against a concurrent `SetInMap` would help too: the asymmetry with `Values()`, which does warn, is what makes this one look safe. Note that `Get` returns the stored value itself, so when that value is a map the caller holds the live map and any read of it has the same exposure. I have kept this report to `GetSortedMapValues` because that one is internal to the type and fixable without changing any signature.

cases.issue_title: panic: slice bounds out of range in contentNodeShifter.Delete when removing draft pages from a multilingual taxonomy
cases.issue_body:
### What version of Hugo are you using?

Reproduced on both:

```
hugo v0.159.1-86c7d3afacab79dc53325602d77ef884b7570268+extended darwin/arm64
hugo v0.164.0+extended+withdeploy darwin/arm64
```

### Does this issue reproduce with the latest release?

Yes (0.164.0).

### What did you expect to see?

A production build (no `-D`) of a multilingual site containing draft pages completes.

### What did you see instead?

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [5:4]

goroutine 37 [running]:
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*contentNodeShifter).Delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x...}, {0x2, 0x0, 0x0})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_contentnodeshifter.go:48 +0x5f4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).delete(0x..., {0x..., 0x35})
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:165 +0x84
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree.(*NodeShiftTree[...]).Delete(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go:107
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages.func1-range1(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:106 +0xa4
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*allPagesAssembler).createAllPages(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go:138 +0x168
github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib.(*HugoSites).assemble(...)
	github.com/gohugoio/hugo/hugolib/hugo_sites_build.go:345 +0x41c
```

The `0x35` in `delete(..., {…, 0x35})` is 53, exactly the byte length of the key being removed (`/blog/` plus a 47-character slug).

### Only on the page-removal path

`hugo -D` (drafts included) builds fine. The panic appears only when a page is *removed* from the tree, which makes it invisible in local preview and fatal only in production.

A **future `publishDate`** panics identically. Setting `[_build] render = "never"` / `list = "never"` on the same pages avoids it entirely — consistent with those pages never being added to the tree, so nothing is deleted.

### What I ruled out

Site: 8 languages, ~1,490 pages per language, ~11,455 content files, `categories` taxonomy.

- **Not a regression.** 0.159.1 and 0.164.0 behave identically.
- **Not the number of drafts.** 96 draft pages build fine; 16 panic.
- **Not slug length.** The panicking key was 47 chars, but renaming an unrelated post to exactly 47 chars builds fine.
- **Not the slug.** Renaming the offending page does not help.
- **Not byte layout.** Deleting a front-matter line, or adding a blank one, still panics.

Swapping page *content* at a fixed path isolates it to **front matter**. Changing `categories = ["Airport Operations"]` on the offending page to any other value clears the panic — and so does moving a *different* page out of that same category while leaving the offending one alone. So the trigger is combinatorial: some particular set of pages being deleted from one taxonomy term corrupts the shifter, rather than any single page being malformed.

### Reproducer

I have not managed to minimise it, and I want to be upfront about that. Synthetic multilingual sites (8 languages, 12 blog + 200 glossary pages sharing one taxonomy term, varying draft counts) do **not** reproduce, so something else in the real tree is required. The affected repository is private.

I am happy to run patches or instrumented builds against the real site and report back, which may be faster than guessing at a minimal case.

cases.issue_title: ReadingTime and FuzzyWordCount have off-by-one errors in their ceiling calculations
cases.issue_body:
## Summary

Two related integer-arithmetic bugs in `hugolib/page__content.go` (in the plain-content calculation), causing behavior that deviates from documented intent at boundary values.

## 1. `ReadingTime` divides by 213/501 instead of 212/500

```go
if isCJKLanguage {
    result.readingTime = (result.wordCount + 500) / 501
} else {
    result.readingTime = (result.wordCount + 212) / 213
}
```

The intent is a reading speed of 212 words per minute (500 for CJK), rounded up. But the correct ceiling-division idiom is `(n + d - 1) / d`. As written, the expression computes `ceil(wordCount / 213)` and `ceil(wordCount / 501)`, so the effective reading speeds are 213 and 501 wpm.

| wordCount | current: `(wc+212)/213` | expected at 212 wpm: `ceil(wc/212)` |
|---|---|---|
| 212 | 1 | 1 |
| 213 | **1** | **2** |
| 424 | 2 | 2 |
| 425 | **2** | **3** |

Proposed fix:

```go
result.readingTime = (result.wordCount + 211) / 212   // non-CJK
result.readingTime = (result.wordCount + 499) / 500   // CJK
```

## 2. `FuzzyWordCount` overshoots on exact multiples of 100

```go
result.fuzzyWordCount = (result.wordCount + 100) / 100 * 100
```

Documented as the word count "rounded up to the nearest multiple of 100", but adding 100 unconditionally bumps exact multiples to the *next* multiple:

| wordCount | current | expected |
|---|---|---|
| 99 | 100 | 100 |
| 100 | **200** | **100** |
| 101 | 200 | 200 |
| 0 | **100** | **0** |

Proposed fix:

```go
result.fuzzyWordCount = (result.wordCount + 99) / 100 * 100
```

Both changes only affect output at exact boundary values, but they do change rendered output for existing sites (e.g., a 100-word page's `FuzzyWordCount` drops from 200 to 100), so this may warrant a changelog note.

	t.Parallel()

-- content/p99.md --
---
title: p99
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 99) + `
-- content/p100.md --
---
title: p100
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 100) + `
-- content/p101.md --
---
title: p101
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 101) + `
-- content/p211.md --
---
title: p211
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 211) + `
-- content/p212.md --
---
title: p212
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 212) + `
-- content/p213.md --
---
title: p213
---
` + strings.Repeat("word ", 213) + `
-- content/p499.md --
---
title: p499
isCJKLanguage: true
---
` + strings.Repeat("你", 499) + `
-- content/p500.md --
---
title: p500
isCJKLanguage: true
---
` + strings.Repeat("你", 500) + `
-- content/p501.md --
---
title: p501
isCJKLanguage: true
---
` + strings.Repeat("你", 501) + `
-- layouts/page.html --
{{ .WordCount }}|{{ .FuzzyWordCount }}|{{ .ReadingTime }}
`

	b := Test(t, files)

	b.AssertFileContent("public/p99/index.html", "99|100|1")
	b.AssertFileContent("public/p100/index.html", "100|100|1") // fails
	b.AssertFileContent("public/p101/index.html", "101|200|1")

	b.AssertFileContent("public/p211/index.html", "211|300|1")
	b.AssertFileContent("public/p212/index.html", "212|300|1")
